A gadget is sensors and inputs that collect data, a processor, outputs, maybe storage and a connection that sends the data on, and power. Every part costs money, battery and space: each choice is a trade-off. Designers read the brief, pick the parts that do the job, test it with real users, and give up what the brief does not need.

Inside a computer every number, letter and picture is kept as tiny switches that are on or off: bits. Counting with bits is called binary. Five switches can make any number from 0 to 31. Storage keeps the switches set even when the power is off.
